assembly.gaps: every inter-phrase gap is gated to true digital silence (adaptive threshold = noise floor p10 + 12 dB, ~18 ms fades) — kills the constant ~91 Hz hum the IndicF5 route leaves in pauses
assembly.level_match: plain gain only — each sentence take is gain-matched to the median speech RMS of the set (no dynamics processing; stacked processing audibly ate the voice identity in audits)
assembly.loudnorm: ONE single-pass ffmpeg loudnorm to approx -15 LUFS at the very end; never stack loudnorm passes

env: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (required) — read from the environment only, never stored here
JULIE_EL_VOICE_ID — or set voice_id in this section
JULIE_TTS_URL (required) — your model server's TTS endpoint
http.request: POST JSON {text, lang, voice}; the response body must be audio bytes (mp3 or wav)

backends.note: Pluggable generation backends (see backends.py). Default per language: en -> chatterbox, te/hi -> indicf5-space. Env JULIE_TTS_BACKEND overrides the route for any language; valid values: indicf5-space | chatterbox | elevenlabs | http. The five gates, the re-roll loop and the QC report apply unchanged on top of every backend, and each take's backend is recorded in the QC report. Keys come from the environment ONLY — no secret values ever live in this file.

english_chatterbox.engine: Chatterbox TTS (Resemble AI, MIT) zero-shot clone

measured_profile.emphasis: word STRETCH on hinge words, NOT pitch drama

pace_guard.action: outside band -> ONE regeneration, then an atempo nudge clamped to 1.12x; what was applied is recorded in the QC report, never silent
pace_guard.metric: onset rate (onsets/second) vs the reference's rate

phrase_chunking.note: Generate phrase by phrase: a unit ends at sentence punctuation (joined with her measured 0.66 s gap) or at a comma/semicolon/colon (joined with 0.06 s — a breath, not a pause). Silences the engine invents INSIDE a phrase are squashed.

gates.note: ALL gates must pass on the SAME take. A sentence with no passing take in max_rolls rolls fails the whole run: the engine exits non-zero with the gate table and writes NO final mp3.
gates.ship_bar_te_hi: EAR-APPROVED BAR (Ajju, 2026-11-16, fixed13 — the first Telugu ear-pass): a te/hi take ships iff gate1 (no-hint language) AND gate2 (ghost scan) pass AND Resemblyzer identity >= identity_min_te_hi AND pace within pace_wps_te_hi, all on the SAME whole take. Gates 3/4/5 are still computed and recorded on every take but are ADVISORY for te/hi: the fixed6 calibration proved the identical suite fails her own genuine narration (g3 min word-prob 0.000-0.326; PHYS flags on real spans), and the ear-approved fixed13 takes do not pass all of g3/g4/g5 (S1 F0 184.2 Hz vs the 185 band edge). ship_decision() in engine.py is the single implementation of this bar; a take that cannot be measured fails closed, and a sentence with no passing take in the roll budget ships NOTHING (exit 2).
gates.whole_take_note: te/hi ship rule (Ajju order 2026-11-16, after the 2026-11-15 ear rejections of fixed2/fixed3/fixed5; bar recalibrated to the ear-approved anchor the same day, fixed13): WHOLE-TAKE ONLY — a te/hi sentence ships only from ONE take passing the ear-approved bar in gates.ship_bar_te_hi (gate1 + gate2 + identity >= identity_min_te_hi + pace within pace_wps_te_hi). No clause/donor assembly, no splice inside a sentence. Roll budgets above local_roll_limit_te_hi are dispatched to the indicf5-batch.yml mass-roll workflow instead of rolling locally.

pace_calibration.how_applied: Generation-side SPEED parameter (fixed10: IndicF5 config.speed scales duration ~1/speed) with the per-ref anchors in speed_anchors, then take SELECTION by the ship bar. atempo / time-stretching on Telugu stays BANNED — it stretched silences and broke the channel rhythm (silence share 25% vs the channel's ~10%).
pace_calibration.owner_ear: -30% speed vs the first sample (Ajju, 2026-11-14); fixed13 natural refs + anchors hit the approved pace with no correction on natspan2 (2026-11-16).

speed_anchors.note: Pre-calibrated IndicF5 generation-speed anchors (fixed13, Actions indicf5-batch, measured 2026-11-16). Store per ref so the first pass lands in the pace band without a calibration wave: natspan2 needs NO correction (speed 1.0 -> S1 6.58 s, S2 9.02 s, both in band); natspan3 runs fast (S1 @0.78 -> 6.92 s, S2 @0.84 -> 8.82 s, both ear-approved). First-pass yield at these anchors: S1 19/20, S2 20/20 takes in band with identity >= 0.85. For a new sentence, start from the ref's anchor and scale by (baseline duration / target duration) if a baseline roll exists (fixed10 rule: duration scales ~1/speed). A ~7% slower variant = anchor x 0.93.
